transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Mike (LumenHealth Lead Eng), Sara (PM), Tom (Security), Aisha (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick sync in middle of POC week 2. Discussed problems with structured output failures in edge cases (JSON serialization errors), fallback model behavior when the preferred model is out of capacity, SDK integration patterns for function/tool calling, and next steps for benchmarks and security artifacts. Some noisy transcription; occasional overlaps.

Topics covered:
- Recent failures in production-like env: intermittent JSON parse errors when agent invokes product-search tool
- How Redwood SDK returns structured output vs raw text and retries/backoff behavior
- Prefix caching interaction with conversation rehydration across restarts
- Security: KMS key rotation, audit log retention, and encryption-in-transit concerns
- Action items and scheduling infra deep-dive

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes on the calendar, quick check-in on the POC integration gaps you flagged last week.
[00:18] Mike (LumenHealth): Yep thanks. We scoped a couple of reproduce cases, the biggest one is when the agent responds with the function payload, occasionally the JSON comes back malformed and then our parser crashes, that was flagged in staging.
[00:32] Priya (SE): Right, we saw that in your trace — looks like trailing commas and sometimes a partial chunk when the connection stalls. Are you using streaming in the SDK or a single response?
[00:44] Mike: We're using the JS SDK wrapper, and we had streaming on for chat, but for function calls we were doing the non-stream path. I think the problem showed up more in higher token responses when we had long index IDs.
[00:59] Sara (PM): To add, the failure is intermittent which makes it harder to reproduce — sometimes clearing the cache helps but not always.
[01:10] Priya: That tracks; two vectors here: one is the SDK's automatic joiner for streamed chunks, the other is how the application re-serializes the response after receiving the "function call" payload. We suggested earlier adding a lightweight validator on receive, but we'll also dig into why fragments arrive.
[01:28] Aisha (DevOps): On our side, we are using a retry wrapper in front of the parser, but when it retries, we get duplicate downstream side effects and idempotency becomes a pain.
[01:40] Jordan: Good note. We should make the retry behavior explicit — Redwood SDK has a configurable safe-retry option and an idempotency token header we can surface. Priya, can you show where that lives in the code?
[01:52] Priya: Yeah I'll pull up the snippet. 
[02:05] Priya: (typing) In the JS client, there's options.retryPolicy.safeRetries and client.call({idempotencyKey}). There's also an example in the quickstart repo for wrapping function-calling responses in a schema validator — I can send that.
[02:22] Mike: That would help. Also curious about fallback model behavior — when your primary model hits capacity we saw a switch but the tokenization/response shape differed and our tool-parsing failed.
[02:34] Jordan: Right — Redwood routing can fallback to a compatible variant but not all variants maintain identical structured output boundaries. We can set a rule to only fall back to variants that pass a lightweight schema check, or to prefer lower-latency cheaper variants flagged as "format-stable".
[02:56] Sara: Is that a config we can control from the dashboard or do we need SE help?
[03:04] Priya: There's a per-route rollout policy. For now we can set the POC route to strictFallback: "format-stable-only" which prevents format-different fallbacks. We can demo that setting and the dashboard toggle.
[03:18] Tom (Security): On the security front, our legal team wants to confirm KMS integration and key ownership. Are keys stored in Redwood or can we bring our own?
[03:28] Jordan: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Hosted POC we have an option to integrate your cloud KMS via disk-encryption-at-rest + envelope encryption. We'll send the architecture diagram.
[03:41] Tom: Also retention. We'd like 30-day verbose audit logs for the POC engine calls, specifically token-level metadata. Is that feasible?
[03:52] Priya: We can extend retention for the trial to 30 days in the console, and produce a short export. For token-level telemetry we may need an extra retention addon — I'll flag that on the next steps.
[04:07] Mike: Back to parsing — we added an example of using a streaming-assembly buffer; but we still see a race where the socket closes mid-chunk. Is there any guarantee about chunk boundaries?
[04:19] Priya: Underlying transport is chunked, not message-delimited, so if the client closes mid-stream you'll get a partial chunk. The JS SDK provides a stable "stream assembler" helper that waits for a final boundary or offers a 'final' flag — but if a hard socket close happens you need to handle incomplete JSON. We can show a snippet.
[04:38] Aisha: Would server-side reassembly and a final validation before forwarding help? We could add a small proxy for now.
[04:45] Jordan: Yup, that's a common pattern during POCs. Use a small proxy to normalize the stream and perform schema validation upstream of the business parser. We'll provide a repo.
[04:58] Sara: There's also the issue of conversation rehydration after our lambda cold-starts — we're losing the KV cache and sometimes re-sending partial prompts which confuses the model state.
[05:12] Priya: For that we suggested persisting a compacted prefix to Redis and then rehydrate. Redwood's prefix caching is idempotent if you store the KV keys and use the same cacheToken. But we saw you had a TTL of 5 minutes — that might be too short for your lambda pattern.
[05:29] Mike: We have short-lived lambdas. Increasing TTL could increase memory cost. Any suggestions on balancing cost vs correctness?
[05:40] Priya: Two options — increase TTL for key user flows (incremental cost), or use a warm-service for rehydration that fetches and primes the cache asynchronously. We'll put both patterns in the repo.
[05:53] Tom: For compliance, does Redwood log the raw prompt content in the audit? We need to avoid storing PII.
[06:02] Jordan: By default, hosted retains prompt and response tokens for telemetry, but we can enable data redaction and configure log filters to strip PII before persistence. For Private deployments data never leaves your VPC unless you opt-in.
[06:18] Tom: Good. Send the redact/filter sample rules.
[06:23] Jordan: Noted.
[06:30] Mike: Quick question — in the last run we saw the SDK returned a 429 but our retry policy retried aggressively and hit a queue that exploded latency. Is there a recommended backoff?
[06:44] Priya: Use exponential backoff with jitter; Redwood SDK default is 250ms base with 2x multiplier and full jitter, capped at 8s. For high-volume streaming calls we recommend a higher cap and an adaptive circuit-breaker tier — we have a sample circuit-breaker config we'll share.
[07:03] Sara: Can you explain how function calling failures are surfaced? We sometimes see a partial function payload and no explicit error.
[07:12] Priya: In that state the SDK emits a 'partial-function' event; we also include a final status code when available. The app should treat partial as a transient and validate the payload before invoking downstream systems. We'll add a boolean 'isComplete' in the example wrapper.
[07:29] Aisha: For our pipelines we want idempotency keys embedded in the function call meta, is that supported?
[07:36] Jordan: Yes, you can set metadata.idempotencyKey and Redwood will return the key in the call event. That ties to the retry handling I mentioned.
[07:45] Mike: Great. Switching topics — we tried toggling quantization in a dedicated internal run and saw odd generation variance affecting structured output. Any guidance?
[07:58] Priya: Quantized variants can shift tokenization boundaries slightly which impacts exact JSON formatting. For strict structured output you should pin to a quantization profile that we've validated for format stability, or run a small acceptance test suite as part of your POC. We can recommend one of our 4-bit profiles that hold format fidelity.
[08:20] Mike: Is there an easy way to assert format stability across variants?
[08:25] Priya: Yes — Redwood Optimize can run a regression check against a prompt set and flag variants that produce schema-drift. We'll run that against your prompt set if you share it.
[08:36] Sara: We'll share the prompt set.
[08:40] Jordan: Perfect. Action items: share SDK snippets, run the benchmarks, share prompt set, schedule infra deep-dive.
[08:50] Priya: One more detail — your app currently expects the function response to be a top-level JSON object. We recommend accepting both rawText and parsedJson in the parser layer to be defensive.
[09:03] Mike: We can do that.
[09:08] Tom: Security follow-ups — what's the process for an SOC2 report and audit evidence if we want to move forward?
[09:16] Jordan: We'll send our SOC2 Type II summary and a Redacted evidence list. For Private deployments we also provide network diagrams and penetration test results.
[09:29] Tom: Okay please share.
[09:33] Priya: I'm going to run a short experiment right now — I have a small test harness that sends a function call with deliberate fragmentation to reproduce the partial chunk. Can I share screen?
[09:42] Mike: Yes go ahead.
[09:45] [screen share noise] Priya: (typing) I'm firing five concurrent requests with streaming enabled. You should see one partial where I drop the socket.
[10:02] Mike: I see the partial event and the SDK emitted a "partial-function" code. The payload has a trailing "}" missing sometimes. That's what kills our parser.
[10:15] Priya: Right so best practice is to wrap the call in the stream-assembler then run a JSON.parse with a small repair pass: if final chunk missing closing brace attempt a lookback for last complete object or return a structured error for downstream safe-failure.
[10:31] Mike: We could add that quick repair.
[10:36] Aisha: If the SDK repair does mutate content do we risk changing semantics?
[10:42] Priya: You should opt for returning an explicit parse error and then let your business logic decide. The repair helper is opt-in for non-critical flows.
[10:51] Jordan: Ok — next up, we should talk about the model fallback policy again — Sara, you mentioned you preferred no silent fallbacks; we can lock to format-stable-only.
[11:02] Sara: That's preferable for the POC. We'll accept a small latency hit rather than broken outputs.
[11:08] Jordan: Great. Priya will set the route policy and send a screenshot.
[11:14] Priya: I'll do that.
[11:18] Mike: Regarding metrics, can we get per-request token counts in the logs? We're trying to reconcile cost.
[11:27] Jordan: Yes — the telemetry include tokens_in/tokens_out per request. For hosted we show that in the console; we'll also export a CSV if you want.
[11:36] Mike: Export please.
[11:38] Jordan: Noted.
[11:45] Tom: For KMS — can you confirm whether Redwood rotates envelope keys and how often?
[11:52] Priya: We rotate envelope keys quarterly by default. For customer-managed HSM you control rotation. We'll add that to the security doc.
[12:02] Tom: Also, can we get a mapping of which logs contain full prompt content so we can set filters?
[12:10] Jordan: We'll provide a matrix.
[12:14] Sara: Anything else before we go into planning?
[12:18] Mike: Quick note: in our last POC run we tried concurrent tool calls and the ordering got interleaved — we need per-session sequencing guarantees.
[12:29] Priya: Redwood doesn't guarantee global ordering across concurrent calls, but per-session sequence IDs are supported. If you attach sessionId the SDK preserves an event order and the server will attach sequence index.
[12:41] Aisha: Perfect. That should cover it.
[12:45] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps and owners. Jordan to send SDK snippets and quickstart, Priya to run benchmarks, Mike to send payloads, Tom to coordinate security artifacts. We'll reconvene next Friday same time.
[13:02] Sara: Works for me.
[13:05] Mike: Thanks all.
[13:07] Jordan: Thanks, bye.
[13:12] [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had trouble with some proper nouns (KMS/HSM, quantization profiles). There is some mild crosstalk during the live screen share at ~09:30-10:10.
